independent.summary: POST /entity-types does not check existing data against a registry that is still empty. In a pre-registry workspace that was never backfilled (the fallback the docs describe), creating one type turns the gate on with only that type. The workspace's existing entities and relationship types then name categories that have no type, which is exactly the drift this item was meant to prevent. Any update that re-sends one of those categories is refused with a 400, and the user cannot delete that one type to go back to the fallback.

When a workspace has no types, the fallback returns true for any name. For Entity the enum still applies. RelationshipType.sourceCategory/targetCategory have no enum, though, so in such a workspace any arbitrary string is accepted. That contradicts the docs and the log line, which say the name is 'checked against the built-in categories'. The fallback should return CATEGORIES.includes(name).

The last-type guard counts the types and then deletes, with nothing locking the two steps together. Two concurrent DELETEs of a workspace's last two types can both see a count of 2 and both succeed. That empties the registry and reopens the enum-only fallback, which the docs say the guard makes impossible. The documented known gap covers only an entity write racing a type delete, not this case.

grades.reason: isRegisteredCategory is the write-time check, not the rename/delete guard; the rename and delete handlers call usesOf(), which does count RelationshipType sourceCategory/targetCategory and returns 409 (the test for deleting alice's Organizations pins this).

This restates the pre-fix bug from the item description, but the merged code fixes it: categoryValidator on Entity.category refuses a name the workspace has no type for on every create and on every workspace-scoped update run with validators, and the test asserts that alice's entity with the deleted Timeline category gets a 400.

summary: The local review found nothing real: one finding points the relationship-type concern at a function that is not the delete guard, and the other restates the original bug, which the diff already fixes. It missed the fallback and race edge cases that remain.
